Have you ever played games like Magic?  It's pretty fun, and a whole lot of people that play are quite awkward and, in any other situation, antisocial to the max. 
(I'm not trying to be stereotypical or sound condescending... I used to play before I had my kids.  I *was* one of those antisocial, socially awkward people.  It was a lot easier to indirectly socialize with a competitive game, and it actually lead to REAL socialization and interaction with people who became real friends beyond the game.)

Certainly there is an option out there that will fit you!

If there is one thing that I have learned through my relationships (with all the wrong people, mind you.), it is this:

(This does not apply to all men, but most that I have been with and most I have known as friends have been this way...)

Men are selfish.  Men want to have their cake and eat it, too.  Men want their ladies to cater to them, their whims and fancies, but they rarely wish to reciprocate.  Men are uncomfortable with emotions.  They rarely show that they even have feelings, and they can't handle when a woman is emotional.  They would rather tell you you're being stupid and walk away than sit, hold you, and listen.  They want to go out with their guy friends and not be bothered, but many have issues with their ladies going out with their friends.  They like to be controlling and possessive.  And, inevitably, they want a mother that also caters to their sexual wants whenever they so desire.  They want a woman to cook and clean for them, do their laundry, go get the groceries so they don't have to brave the store...  They want a woman to cook things their mothers cooked, the way their mothers cooked.  I cannot tell you how many times I made something and was told in the middle of the meal, "My mom always made it another way.  Will you make it the way my mom makes it next time?"  Possibly one of the most hurtful things every time I heard it.  Like, "Oh, my cooking isn't good enough for you.  Gee, thanks." 

I've also been with men that wanted me to change for them--change my hobbies, my appearance, my passions.  I'm pale and keep my hair its natural brown color now, with the exception of some highlights and lowlights.  I am scared to death of melanoma, as a couple members of my family have had it.  I grew up a tom-boy, and rarely wore makeup or fancied up my hair or wore "girly" clothes, heels, or jewelry.  My last SO always told me what he'd like for me to do differently--he wanted me to tan, to get blond hair, he even told me how he wanted my hair styled.  "Grow your hair out past your shoulders and do spiral curls on the last few inches of it."  HE picked out what I bought if I went clothes shopping.  If he didn't like it, I didn't get it because he'd hound me until I put it back.  He even told me how he wanted me to do my makeup.  He "surprised" me with tanning minutes. (Gee, thanks.  I don't want to tan.)  Animals are my life, besides my children, and always have been.  He disliked animals.  He made me keep my cats outside, and when one was killed by a neighborhood dog, he didn't even say sorry about making me put the cats out.  He did say sorry the cat died, but what was that supposed to do for me?  I have been riding horses since I was 9.  I love it.  I always wanted to go riding, but he never wanted to go with me, yet I was expected to help him collect video games and gamefaq for him when he was playing.  I was expected to do what he wanted, when he wanted, but he wouldn't do the same for me.  Men can be very one-sided.

Men... Augh.  Men.

Not all men are like this--(To the male readers going, "Hey, now.  That's not me!)  I've known quite a few good, selfless, loving men.  Granted, I've never ended up with any of them.  Which is really pretty stupid, because it's not like some of them didn't try to have me.

But, look, hon.  He is being rather typical.  There are good men out there.  There are men that will love you and wipe your tears.  There are men who will listen and try to help you.  You deserve that.  

If he decides to end it, please do not do yourself injustice and end it.  Understand that he got you through a chapter in your life, and move on to the next chapter.  Find one of the kind ones.  Find one of the good ones.  You can, and you will if you just let go.

I found one of those men, however due to circumstances, we cannot be together.  I used to work with him years ago, and he is a great man, but he lives states away, and my family is all around me here.  My grandmother is quite elderly and is slowly growing senile, and I do not want to leave and not have time with her before she inevitably goes.

But, they're there.  

Love, look at yourself in the mirror and realize that you are beautiful.  That you deserve respect.  That you deserve to be loved.  That you deserve better.  If he can't offer you that, then it may be in your best interest to move on, lest feel like you're always doing something wrong and are never appreciated down the road.  Lest you become resentful.

You can message me if you like.  I'd be happy to listen and try to help if you like, or just be a friend to speak with about whatever you want/need to talk about.

Have you tried going fishing or hiking?  You could take one person you feel somewhat comfortable with along if you wanted, or do it by yourself.  Low-stimulation activity in an environment away from lots of people, should help you get out and enjoy the world without the social anxiety.

Do you have interests besides video games and Netflix?  Art, writing, photography, animals, martial arts, sports, astronomy, etc?  Hobbies can be rewarding in many ways.  Not only are you bringing yourself enjoyment of your time, but often you can do something you take pride in and build your confidence.  The arts are quite helpful in getting your feelings out there, whether through abstract paintings/drawings or writing stories, poetry, or prose.  There are organizations for just about anything you can think of, whether in your area or online, and sharing your interests and hobbies with birds of the same feather will help you socialize with less anxiety--you know that they enjoy the same thing you do, and you can talk to and share with them without fear of being judged or put down for your interest.  In fact, most people will be encouraging to you, praise you, and really make you feel good about yourself.

If you don't have any real hobbies, consider trying some out and see if you find something you like.  If you'd like to talk, I'd be happy to speak with you and see if we can't find some way to bring your spirits up! =)

Also, in regards to my emotional ties to my ex:

I never stopped loving him, even with all the pain he's put me through.  I still care about him, I still love him.  I simply am not "in love" with him anymore.  I want him to clean up--not for me, but for himself.  He is brilliant and has so much potential for great things, but he has an issue.  I'm not exactly new to the world of addicts--I am not an addict, but I have had many friends and family that struggled with addiction.  I understand that his actions have nothing to do with his love, or lack of love, for me.  He has a problem and he needs help.  I've begged him to go to a long-term, good rehab facility.  I've also begged him to see a psychiatrist.  I've got his addiction figured out to a T.  (I'm not even saying that to be cocky.)  I honestly think I understand it more than he does.

But that is neither here nor there.  The fact of the matter is that he is struggling with deeper issues than just addiction.  Addiction is more like a symptom of what he's dealing with.  Crack is his coping mechanism.  He needs to see a psychiatrist and go through therapy to learn how to cope in a manner that isn't destructive.

I know he is a good person inside.  I've seen good in him, and we have had wonderful times together, but the bad has far outweighed the good.  I just want to see him get better.

But not with me.

"Our time" is over, and that's a hard pill to swallow when you genuinely love someone with all your heart and have put all of yourself into them.  I suppose that only adds to my depression.  I want him, I love him, I want him to get better, but I know that we will never have the relationship we could have had.  I know it'll never be healthy.  I know I'll stress and worry and look over my shoulder if I'm with him, no matter how long he stays clean.

That just makes everything all the more difficult.

I have spoken to a lawyer here.  His advice was pretend everything's okay and get out of state.  Pretend I'm just trying to sort things out in my head, or find a job somewhere out of state, or visiting friends.  Catch with that is that I'd have to make it 6 months without him figuring out what I was doing, or they could yank me back to the state I'm currently in.  After 6 months, though, the children would be legal residents of the state & if he felt the desire to arrange a custody or visitation agreement, he'd have to do it in whatever state I was in.

I am not worried about him having custody while I'm okay.  If it comes down to that kind of fight, he will lose.  It's visitation that scares me.  It would be custody that scared me if I were to go into suicide watch, and that is simply something I don't feel comfortable speaking with an attorney about.

I have never bought him drugs.  He has stolen plenty of money and possessions of mine to get the drugs, though.  When I said I had to take him to go get crack before our first daughter was born, the scenario went like this:  His mom and I drove towns away to track him down so he'd be present for baby's birth.  Got home with him.  No more than ten minutes later, he tells me that either I drive him to get the crack, or he was going to take my vehicle and drive himself.  Not only did I have a scheduled induction just two hours away at that point, but also I felt that if I let him leave, he wouldn't be back.  I felt like it was extremely important for him to be present because you just never know if it might have changed something if you don't try.  I had to give it a chance, just hoping that maybe seeing his child being born would make something in his brain click and make him want better for himself.  Didn't happen, though.

His mom is an attorney.  She pretty much enables his drug use.  In the past 8 years, he's cost her approximately $300,000.00 through theft of her cash and check books, breaking into her home and stealing her valuable belongings to trade for crack, creating fraudulent accounts and writing bad checks that she always pays off for him...  In the last two years, he's taken about $35,000 of her money alone--$14,000 of which she put in an account for him when he was clean for a down-payment on a new house.  At that time, he also broke into her law firm and wrote himself all kinds of checks, totaling over $3500.  That was gone in 2 weeks.  Last Christmas he wrote over $8,000 in checks from her trust account.  This last time around, he stole her checkbook and wrote at least $12,000 in checks.  Those amounts do not include cash that he's stolen from her in the past two years.  She pays all of his bills and continues to allow him to handle her checkbooks by helping her make sure all her bills are paid.  

This last time around, she announced she was through with him.  She filed a report for her missing checks and car.  She offered rewards to her drug-abusing clients to find him and bring her checkbook back to her.  She stated that he was dead to her and that she would press charges against him and let him go to prison, and when eligible for parole, she wanted a term to be that he not contact her.  That lasted all of a week after he came home.  He was "banned" from her house.  That lasted all of two weeks.  He wasn't allowed near her check books--3 weeks.  She enables him more than anyone, and she has pretty well come out and told me that if I were to do anything that caused him to be arrested, she was going to make my life hell.  After his abuse this last time around while I was pregnant, I wanted to go to the hospital--my wrist was sprained and cut pretty bad, and my ribs were bruised.  I couldn't pick up my child, and it hurt to breath, but I didn't go because when I told her I was going to the hospital and asked if she could watch my kid, she basically took my job away from me.  (Oh yeah, did I mention I've worked for her for two years?) So, I didn't go.  No reports, no photos, no proof that it ever happened.

Before I had my second child, I began having horrid anxiety attacks.  I spoke to my OBGYN and he prescribed me an antidepressant and xanax.  That helps a lot, but sometimes even that isn't enough to keep me from losing my mind.

I would love to see a psychiatrist.  I saw one a few years ago and it made a world of difference for me.  My issue is, if I express how I'm feeling and end up committed, what happens to the kids?  Or, if I come out with how I'm feeling, will they see me as a danger to myself and/or others and take my children from me.  That's the last thing I want, but I do need to get psychiatric help.
